title: Exact bitmap BF through CM compress offset
reasons: no visible template faster beyond its noise (best: q09 -3.9%; needs at least -8.6%)
summary:
Join filters can now push the exact-bitmap Bloom filter through compressed-materialization integral compression (__internal_compress_integral_*(x, off)). Before this, only shifted min/max and range-set filters went through; the BF was skipped.
- bloom_filter.hpp/.cpp: BFTableFilter gets has_key_offset/key_offset (SetKeyOffset), carried over in Copy. In exact mode the probe looks up widen(scanned value) - key_offset, with 64-bit wrapping. Widening is sign-extend for signed and zero-extend for unsigned storage types. The same shift is applied in Filter, FilterValue and CheckStatistics. CheckStatistics uses a separate offset version: it maps [min,max] to a contiguous arc of bitmap positions and prunes only if the arc doesn't wrap and lies entirely past the bitmap range; otherwise it probes each value when the range is ≤2048. If a filter has an offset but isn't exact, it lets every row pass.
- physical_hash_join.cpp: FinalizeFilters has a new branch. It applies when storage_offset is set, the filter is on join key 0, CanUseBloomFilter holds, and the offset converts to 64 bits (TryGetExactKeyOffset; storage type must be an integer of 64 bits or less). In that case it runs the exact gate on the raw compressed-key min/max before Finalize fills the bitmap. Only if that makes the filter exact does it turn on the BF build and defer the push. PushBloomFilter finds the probe column for key 0; if it has an offset, it pushes only when the filter is exact and has no overflow, using the storage type as key_type and setting key_offset. A hashed BF is never pushed through an offset.
Measured: q09 orders scan went from 15M to 2.94M rows. Bench q09 -9.2% / -9.0% (534→485, 514→468 ms). Full-suite geomean -0.3%. q04 showed +7.4% in the first run and -6.8% when rerun (noise); everything else within noise.
Correctness: TEMP tables with a 30M-row probe (with NULL keys) and a 15M-row build filtered to 10%, where CM compresses both join sides. Tested BIGINT keys starting at 1e9 (offset 1e9), negative BIGINT keys (−1e12−i), UBIGINT keys starting at 3e9, and a RIGHT join. All results equal those with SET disabled_optimizers='join_filter_pushdown'. EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows probe scans dropping from 30M to 3M rows for the positive and negative BIGINT cases; the UBIGINT and RIGHT-join scan counts were not checked.
notes: The exact gate must use the raw (compressed) min/max from final_min_max. min_val/max_val in FinalizeFilters have already been converted to storage values with the offset added. In my tests CM compressed only BIGINT/UBIGINT keys; INTEGER keys weren't compressed, so the offset path didn't run for them. To get CM on a join in temp-table tests you need a build of about 15M rows. q09 orders HJ CPU remains roughly build-side bound (3.27M inserts). Serialization of key_offset was not added: BF deserialization already creates a detached filter. Possible follow-up: q05/q07/q08 didn't move measurably, so CM-under-join with a dense key is mostly a q09 pattern in this workload.
